digest.component_or_area: Git fetch coordination in rebar store sync and snapshot paths
propositions: Parallel Git fetches against a shared common directory race on remote-tracking ref updates without coordinated locking, causing compare-and-swap mismatch failures (cannot lock ref: is at <new> but expected <old>).

The sync fetch in reconverge and snapshot fetch in fetch_origin run outside the ticket write lock and use per-operation locks that do not coordinate with each other, allowing concurrent ref-update collisions.

The failure occurs deterministically with parallel execution (82/128 failures) and reliably reproduces zero failures with serialized execution, confirming a race mechanism rather than network or state corruption.

Both sync and snapshot paths must coordinate fetches via a cross-process lock keyed on the canonical Git common directory (following commondir pointers and realpath for linked worktrees) without blocking the ticket write lock.

A residual race with non-rebar Git processes requires bounded retry on ref CAS mismatch, with sync continuing best-effort (skip round) and snapshot failing closed with actionable error after exhaustion.

The explicit tickets destination refspec and narrow-clone requirements must be preserved, network fetches must not hold the write lock, and concurrency documentation must name the fetch coordination and recovery policy.
